div.head: Northu 35
div.ab: Gif preost cwenan forlæte ⁊ oðre nime, anathema sit!
Gif preost cwenan forlæte and oðre nime, anathema sit!
Wenn ein Priester [seine] Frau verlässt und eine andere nimmt, Anathema sit!
If a priest leaves [his] woman and takes another, let him be anathema!
If a priest leaves a woman and takes another, let him be anathema!
If a priest abandons one woman and takes another, let him be accursed!
div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.

note.label: contrast
note.quote: Northu. 35; compare (e.g.) VI Atr 5:1-2 ... where it is an aggravation of an already serious offence that priests have more than one wife

div.note: Liebermann compares VI Atr 5.2.; AU: corrected against Rabin p. 308 / 309, October 2026 (was “Gif preost cwenan forlæte and oðre nime, anathema sit!”, now “Gif preost cwenan forlæte and oðre nime, anathema sit! (expanded letters in italics: anathema sit)”); W: corrected against Rabin p. 309, October 2026 (was “If a priest abandons one woman and takes another, let him be accursed!”, now “If a priest abandons one woman and takes another, let him be accursed! (expanded letters in italics: let him be accursed!)”)
This clause’s condemnation of a priest abandoning his wife marks a significant departure from Wulfstan’s thought. For Wulfstan, all clerical marriage was anathema, regardless of circumstance.

note.seg: cwene kann neben ‘Frau allgemein oder im schlechten Sinne’ auch ‘Ehefrau’ heissen. Letztere ist hier gemeint, laut der Quelle, und weil nicht das Verheiratetsein, sondern das Wechseln der Frau verdammt wird; vgl. Gl Cölibat 3—4. Dennoch mag vielleicht absichtlich das eindeutige Wort für Ehefrau, æwe u. 65, hier gemäss strengerer Kanonistik vermieden sein

Besides ‘woman in general, or in a bad sense’, cwene can also mean ‘wife’. The latter is meant here, according to the source, and because what is condemned is not being married but changing one’s wife; cf. Gl Cölibat 3—4. Nevertheless the unambiguous word for wife, æwe below 65, may perhaps have been deliberately avoided here in keeping with stricter canon law

note.label: woman
note.seg: Though marriage of the clergy had to be tolerated, cwene is not a usual term for a legal wife.
